claims.text: Adding approximately 2 wt% Cr to the Cu matrix will promote formation of a Cr-enriched graded interphase at W/Cu boundaries.
The Cr-enriched interphase will suppress W–Cu phase separation.
The Cr-enriched interphase will suppress interfacial void formation under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
A W–Cu composite containing approximately 2 wt% Cr in its Cu matrix will have higher effective thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable untreated W–Cu composite.
Cr will segregate to W–Cu interfaces during composite processing.
Cr segregation will reduce W/Cu interfacial energy and stabilize the interface.
The graded Cr-enriched interphase will suppress the nucleation of interfacial voids.
The graded Cr-enriched interphase will suppress the growth of interfacial voids.
A well-bonded Cr-modified W/Cu interface will minimize phonon scattering.
Reduced interfacial phonon scattering will enhance thermal conductivity under applied heat and irradiation.
The Cr-doped composite will exhibit fewer interfacial voids than the untreated composite under comparable high-heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The Cr-doped composite will exhibit less phase separation than the untreated composite under comparable high-heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Untreated W–Cu composites develop phase separation and interfacial voids under relevant thermal and irradiation loads.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation cause poorer thermal conductivity in the untreated composite.
The intervention requires processing temperatures that permit controlled Cr diffusion.
Excessive interdiffusion at sufficiently severe service conditions may produce unwanted phase transformations.
